newsitem.title: USA: Dozens held hostage for hours in Philadelphia.
newsitem.headline: Dozens held hostage for hours in Philadelphia.

text.p: More than 100 people were held hostage for several hours on Friday in an apparent botched robbery attempt at a cash-checking business in northeast Philadelphia, police said.
Deputy Philadelphia police commissioner Richard Zappile told reporters as many as eight robbers were involved in the hostage drama, which ended without any serious injuries.

Police spokesman Corp. Jim Pauley said all the hostages were believed to have been released from the Financial Exchange check cashing business. "It appears that way, but we're not sure," Pauley told Reuters.

A Philadelphia police officer accidentally shot himself in the hand during the tense standoff with the thieves and a pregnant woman was reported to have been taken to the hospital. No other injuries were reported.
Zappille said the incident began on Thursday night.

Media reports said an employee of the Financial Exchange, where residents can cash checks, pick up food stamps and obtain other financial services, was kidnapped and held overnight at her home at gunpoint with her family.
The woman was then brought to the business in an attempt to gain entrance and apparently rob an armoured car.
However, the robbery did not go as planned and customers arriving at the business were not allowed to leave, Pauley said. Police were alerted at 10:15 a.m. EST (1515 GMT).
After a stand-off with police lasting several hours, the hostage-takers allowed dozens of captives -- including women and children -- to slowly file out of the building.
"If we get out of this situation with just one officer shot in the hand, it's a tremendous victory," Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell told a Philadelphia NBC television affiliate.

The hostages were searched and questioned by police, who separated captives from robbers. The released hostages were then transported by police to a site where they would be interviewed. Medical emergency vehicles were on the scene.

Sam Little, whose wife was the 14th hostage freed, told a local NBC affiliate he was "ecstatic" at her release. He said the businesses were known to have a large amount of cash on hand and his wife and other residents feared it would be a robbery target.
"These places are just setting themselves up to get robbed like this," he said.
